name: ACLU Foundation
mission: The American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) Foundation is the arm of the ACLU that conducts litigation and communication efforts. The Foundation provides legal representation in cases involving issues of civil liberties and constitutional rights, ranging from administrative hearings to trials and appeals. In addition, the Foundation educates the public as to civil liberties and constitutional rights by disseminating literature and other publications. The ACLU Foundation preserves and promotes civil rights and liberties as guaranteed by the United States Constitution.
programs: Trone Center for Justice and Equality
theoryOfChange: The American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU) Foundation has a published 'TVTP Grant Program Logic Model' on its website. This document, released on December 15, 2022, serves as a logic model for a specific grant program, outlining the program's intended structure and approach.

rich_narrative.summary: The ACLU Foundation operates as a major legal advocacy organization working to defend civil liberties across the United States. Key limiting factors for donors include <cite id="1">excessive working capital reserves</cite> holding over 40 months of operating funds and a revenue contraction in recent years. In FY2025, the charity reported <cite id="2">Total Revenue of $306,750,536</cite> with a <cite id="2">Program expense ratio of 83.5%</cite>. Organizationally, financial efficiency remains solid as fundraising cost <cite id="1">only $0.12 per $1 raised</cite> in FY2025. It holds a <cite id="1">100/100 rating from Charity Navigator</cite> based on standard accountability metrics, though its revenue declined from $201,181,635 in FY2023 to $185,146,988 in FY2024.
